title: Bootstrapping (computing)
summary: Bootstrapping in computing describes self-starting processes that proceed without external input. It encompasses creating self-compiling compilers, initializing computer software through a staged chain from hardware procedures to operating systems, and developing complex programming environments from basic tools. In simulation research, bootstrapping initializes models using pseudorandom data to establish event sequences that converge toward steady-state distributions over time.

mechanisms.title: Compiler self-hosting
mechanisms.explanation: A compiler is first built in an existing language, then rewritten in the new language and compiled by itself, enabling the language to 'pull itself up by its bootstraps' to full functionality.

mechanisms.title: Simulation initialization via pseudorandom data
mechanisms.explanation: Discrete-event simulation models are bootstrapped by using a pseudorandom number generator to schedule an initial set of events; over time, the event distribution approaches steady state, overwhelming the initial bootstrapping behavior.
